en: Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa. Oṃ. Of this mantra of the Śrī Gopālahṛdayastotra, the venerable Lord Saṅkarṣaṇa is the seer (ṛṣi);
the Gāyatrī is the meter (chandaḥ); Oṃ is the seed-syllable (bīja); Lakṣmī is the power (śakti); and Gopāla, the Supreme Self, is the deity (devatā).

Pradyumna is the *kīlaka*. For the purpose of destroying all sins accumulated through mind, speech, and body, and for the sake of pleasing Śrī Gopāla, this is the application (*viniyoga*) for the recitation of the *Gopālahṛdaya-stotra*.
Śrī Saṅkarṣaṇa said:
Oṃ: May Viṣṇu always be before me, and Keśava also behind me;
may Govinda be at my right side, and Madhusūdana at my left. (1)
May Vaikuṇṭha protect from above, may Vārāha protect upon the surface of the earth,
and may Mādhava protect in all the intermediate directions.
Whether walking or standing, waking or even sleeping, there is protection from Narasiṃha; for he is composed of Vāsudeva.
They say that his source is the unmanifest, while his body is the manifest; his long life is his course.
Fire is his mouth, the moon and sun are his eyes, the quarters are his ears, and the wind is his breath and his life-force.

One should know that his speech is the Vedas, his heart is the sky, his feet are the earth, and the pores of his skin are the stars; his limbs and minor members are the presiding deities, and likewise, his generative organ is the ocean.

Salutations to you, the God of gods, the refuge of all creatures, whose essence is sacrifice, the foundation of all worlds; the unborn, the most excellent, the giver of boons, the supreme, the Brahman, the Lord, the Puruṣa. 6.
The primordial Person, the Lord, invoked by many, placed at the forefront—the Truth, the single-syllabled Brahman, manifest yet unattached, eternal. (7)
One who glorifies the narrative of the Mahābhārata, Kurukṣetra, the Sarasvatī river, Keśava, the cow, and the Gaṅgā— toward me he becomes gracious.

Oṃ bhūḥ! Salutations again and again to Vāsudeva, the Puruṣa, who has the form of Puruṣa. Oṃ bhuvaḥ! Salutations again and again to Vāsudeva, the Puruṣa, who has the form of Puruṣa. Oṃ svaḥ! Salutations again and again to Vāsudeva, the Puruṣa, who has the form of Puruṣa.
Oṃ, salutations again and again to Vāsudeva, the Great Puruṣa, who has the form of the Puruṣa. Oṃ, salutations again and again to Vāsudeva, the Janaloka Puruṣa, who has the form of the Puruṣa.
Oṃ, salutations again and again to Vāsudeva, the Tapoloka Puruṣa, who has the form of the Puruṣa.

Oṃ, salutation again and again to Vāsudeva, the Truth, the Supreme Person, who has the form of the Supreme Person. Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, salutation again and again to Vāsudeva, the Supreme Person, who has the form of the Supreme Person. Oṃ, salutation again and again to Vāsudeva, the Supreme Person, who has the form of the Supreme Person.

Oṃ, salutations again and again to Saṅkarṣaṇa, the Puruṣa, whose form is that of Puruṣa, Vāsudeva. Oṃ, salutations again and again to Pradyumna, the Puruṣa, whose form is that of Puruṣa, Vāsudeva. Oṃ, salutations again and again to Aniruddha, the Puruṣa, whose form is that of Puruṣa, Vāsudeva.

Oṃ, salutations again and again to Hayagrīva, the Supreme Person, who has the form of the Supreme Person, Vāsudeva. Oṃ, salutations again and again to Bhava, the one beyond becoming, the Supreme Person, who has the form of the Supreme Person, Vāsudeva. Oṃ, salutations again and again to Keśava, the Supreme Person, who has the form of the Supreme Person, Vāsudeva.

Oṃ, salutations again and again to Nārāyaṇa, the Puruṣa, whose form is that of the Puruṣa, Vāsudeva. Oṃ, salutations again and again to Mādhava, the Puruṣa, whose form is that of the Puruṣa, Vāsudeva. Oṃ, salutations again and again to Govinda, the Puruṣa, whose form is that of the Puruṣa, Vāsudeva.

Oṃ, salutations again and again to Viṣṇu, the Supreme Person, whose form is that of the Puruṣa, Vāsudeva. Oṃ, salutations again and again to Madhusūdana, the Supreme Person, whose form is that of the Puruṣa, Vāsudeva. Oṃ, salutations again and again to Vaikuṇṭha, the Supreme Person, whose form is that of the Puruṣa, Vāsudeva.

Oṃ, obeisance again and again to Acyuta, the Supreme Person, who has the form of the Person, Vāsudeva. Oṃ, obeisance again and again to Trivikrama, the Supreme Person, who has the form of the Person, Vāsudeva. Oṃ, obeisance again and again to Vāmana, the Supreme Person, who has the form of the Person, Vāsudeva.

Oṃ, salutations again and again to Śrīdhara, the Supreme Person, who has the form of the Supreme Person, Vāsudeva. Oṃ, salutations again and again to Hṛṣīkeśa, the Supreme Person, who has the form of the Supreme Person, Vāsudeva. Oṃ, salutations again and again to Padmanābha, the Supreme Person, who has the form of the Supreme Person, Vāsudeva.

Oṃ, salutations again and again to Mukunda, the Supreme Person, whose form is that of the Puruṣa, Vāsudeva. Oṃ, salutations again and again to Dāmodara, the Supreme Person, whose form is that of the Puruṣa, Vāsudeva. Oṃ, salutations again and again to Satya, the Supreme Person, whose form is that of the Puruṣa, Vāsudeva.

Oṃ, salutations again and again to Īśāna, to Puruṣa, to him who has the form of Puruṣa, to Vāsudeva. Oṃ, salutations again and again to Tatpuruṣa, to Puruṣa, to him who has the form of Puruṣa, to Vāsudeva. Oṃ, salutations again and again to Puruṣottama, to Puruṣa, to him who has the form of Puruṣa, to Vāsudeva.

Oṃ, salutations again and again to Śrī Rāmacandra, the Supreme Person, whose form is that of the Puruṣa, Vāsudeva. Oṃ, salutations again and again to Śrī Nṛsiṃha, the Supreme Person, whose form is that of the Puruṣa, Vāsudeva. Oṃ, salutations again and again to Ananta, the Supreme Person, whose form is that of the Puruṣa, Vāsudeva.

Oṃ, salutations again and again to Vāsudeva, the one of universal form, the Supreme Person, whose form is the Person. Oṃ, salutations again and again to Vāsudeva, the Supreme Person, whose form is the Person, who possesses the Praṇava, the moon, fire, the sun, and a thousand eyes.
Whoever studies this Gopālahṛdaya becomes purified from the murder of a Brahmin;

he becomes purified from the drinking of liquor, from the theft of gold, from sexual intercourse with a low-caste woman, from conversing with one's husband [inappropriately], from untruthfulness, from approaching those who should not be approached, from drinking what should not be drunk, and from eating what should not be eaten.
"One who does not practice celibacy becomes a practitioner of celibacy," said the Blessed Lord Mahāviṣṇu.
Thus ends the Gopālahṛdayastotra.
